title: find_available_port races between probe and bind
description:
The port chosen by `find_available_port` is released before the caller binds it, so any process that grabs it in between makes the caller fail. The workspace test suite hits this as a flaky failure under parallel load.

## Background

`crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:249` probes a port by binding a `TcpListener`, drops the listener when `is_ok()` returns, and hands the bare port number back:

```rust
(start..=start.saturating_add(99))
    .find(|&port| TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).is_ok())
```

The returned port is unowned by the time the caller sees it. `jit serve` then binds it a second time, and that second bind can fail even though the probe succeeded.

`test_find_available_port_returns_free_port` (`serve.rs:712`) reproduces the window: it calls `find_available_port(3000)`, then binds the result. Observed failing once in a full parallel `cargo test` run and passing when run alone. The sibling test `test_find_available_port_skips_bound_port` binds ports in the same range concurrently, which is one of the racing parties.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: The port-selection API hands the caller an owned, already-bound listener rather than a port number the caller must re-bind.
- [hard] REQ-2: `jit serve` binds exactly once; no code path re-binds a port that a probe reported as free.
- [hard] REQ-3: The port-selection tests pass deterministically under parallel execution, and no test in the suite binds a fixed port range that a sibling test also binds.

## Notes

Returning `TcpListener` instead of `u16` closes the window at the type level. Discovered during epic dbe1e821 execution by a rework agent whose full-suite run failed on this test and passed on rerun; the flake is a symptom, the unowned-port handoff is the defect.
